+# In-game master volume control (proof of concept)
+
+- `START + R1`: increase the game master volume by 5 percentage points.
+- `START + R2`: decrease it by 5 percentage points.
+- The initial scale is relative to master-volume values captured on the first change; 0% mutes, 100% preserves the baseline, and up to 150% is requested.
+
+The EE-side IGR polling thread sends the requested percentage over SIF RPC to the IOP module. OPL embeds `volctrl.irx` into its module storage and attempts to load it after IOP initialization. The service uses LIBSD master-volume parameters for both SPU2 cores.
+
+## Validation status
+
+This is an uncompiled proof of concept. Button-byte masks, LIBSD parameter encoding, RPC imports and behavior across games must be checked against the exact PS2SDK toolchain and on real hardware. Games may reconfigure their master volume, and titles that reboot the IOP may unload the service. Do not treat it as a release build.

@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+# In-game volume overlay (experimental)
+
+This branch is derived from `feature/in-game-volume-control` and adds a compact on-screen volume indicator when START+R1 or START+R2 changes the requested volume.
+
+## Expected behavior
+
+- The indicator is placed near the upper-right corner of the currently scanned-out GS framebuffer.
+- It displays `VOL`, the requested percentage, and a horizontal 0–150% bar.
+- It is redrawn for up to 90 successful frame polls (roughly 1.5–1.8 seconds at common refresh rates).
+- The renderer supports GS PSMCT32, PSMCT24, PSMCT16 and PSMCT16S. Other display formats cause the indicator to disable itself for that appearance.
+
+## Important limitations
+
+This is a proof of concept, not a release-ready OSD. It transfers pixels into the active framebuffer through VIF1/GIF. It checks for a busy VIF1 path and avoids changing the game's drawing-context registers, but game-specific DMA scheduling, framebuffer flipping, interlaced output, and GS pixel formats still need validation on real hardware. The transfer path is shared with game rendering, so even with the idle check there is a race window; flicker, rendering interference, or a game-specific failure is possible.
+
+No build or hardware test has been run in this environment. Keep this branch separate and do not merge it until it has built with the intended PS2SDK, been tested on at least one game in each relevant display mode, and shown that graphics/audio and IGR remain stable. The base volume-control code also remains an uncompiled proof of concept.

commit.message:
cheatman: ignore comment lines that start with blanks

A .cht line such as " //Gameplay 16:9" is cut at "//" by term_str(),
which leaves " ". trim_str() returned early for a string without
printable characters and kept it as is, so parse_buf() took " " as a
cheat name. In "select cheats" mode the codes after such a comment
showed up as an unnamed entry instead of belonging to the previous
cheat, as they do when the comment starts in column 0.

trim_str() now empties a blank string, so the line is skipped like any
other comment.

Reproduction: SLES_505.41.cht and SLES_539.08.cht from
PS2-Widescreen/OPL-Widescreen-Cheats. Before: "Mastercode" (1 code)
plus a cheat named " " (7 codes). After: "Mastercode" with 8 codes, as
for a comment in column 0. The other 3,609 files in that repository
parse the same before and after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cheatman: stop at MAX_CODES cheats instead of writing past gCheats

parse_buf() tested "cheat_index < MAX_CODES" before incrementing
cheat_index, so the 251st cheat in a file was written to
gCheats[MAX_CODES], one entry past the array.

RiptOPL fixed the overflow by testing "cheat_index + 1 < MAX_CODES"
(NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@8a2e8743). With that test alone the
codes of each further cheat are still stored, in the last cheat: its
code index restarts at 0 for every name, so they replace that cheat's
own codes. Stop parsing instead once the table is full.

Reproduction: a .cht file with 251 cheats of one code each, parsed by a
host build of parse_buf().
- Before: AddressSanitizer reports a write past the end of gCheats.
- With only the index test: cheat 250 gets the code of cheat 251.
- After: 250 cheats, each with its own code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cheatman: make room for the terminator in make_code()

make_code() is only called for lines that is_cheat_code() accepted,
which have exactly CODE_DIGITS (16) hex digits. It copies them into
char digits[CODE_DIGITS] and then writes the terminating NUL to
digits[16], one byte past the array, for every cheat code it parses.

The same fix is in RiptOPL (NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@8a2e8743).

Reproduction: any .cht file with a code line, parsed by a host build of
parse_buf(). Before: AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow
in make_code(), and an MSVC build with /GS aborts with
STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN. After: no report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cheatman: do not run past the last line of a .cht file

When the last line of a .cht file has no LF, parse_buf():
- skipped the CHEAT_LINE_MAX cap, which was only applied to lines that
  end with LF, so a last line longer than 255 bytes was copied past
  line[256] on the stack;
- advanced by len + 1, past the terminating NUL, and went on parsing
  whatever followed the buffer on the heap.

Cap every line, and step over the byte after a line only when it is not
the terminator. Long lines that end with LF are handled as before.

RiptOPL fixed both (NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@8a2e8743).

Reproduction, on a host build of parse_buf():
- 27 of the 3,611 files in PS2-Widescreen/OPL-Widescreen-Cheats end
  without LF (e.g. SCES_503.00.cht). Before: AddressSanitizer reports a
  heap-buffer-overflow read on each. After: no report, same cheats.
- A file ending with a 400-byte line without LF. Before: stack-buffer-
  overflow write in parse_buf(). After: the line is cut at 255 bytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

isofs, cdvdman: skip directory records without a name

cdvdman_locatefile() advanced to the next directory record only inside
"if (filename_len)". A record with a non-zero length and a name length
of 0 therefore never moved tocPos, and the scan looped forever. The
game list (isofs) hangs on such an image while it looks for
SYSTEM.CNF; the in-game CDVDMAN copy hangs on the first file lookup.

Advance past every record that is neither the match nor the directory
to descend into.

Reproduction: a root directory with ".", "..", a 34-byte record whose
name length is 0, then SYSTEM.CNF;1, fed to host builds of both copies
of cdvdman_locatefile(). Before: endless loop. After: SYSTEM.CNF;1 is
found.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

isofs, cdvdman: read the directory record length as one byte

struct dirTocEntry declared the first two bytes of a directory record
as one short. In ISO 9660 (9.1.1, 9.1.2) byte 0 is the record length
and byte 1 is the extended attribute record length. A non-zero byte 1
made cdvdman_locatefile() step by 256 bytes or more, and a value of
0x80 or more made the step negative, so the scan read before
cdvdman_buf and could loop forever.

Split the field into two bytes and step by the record length alone.
cdrom_dread() in the in-game CDVDMAN uses the same struct and now steps
the same way. Records with byte 1 = 0, which is what mastering tools
write, are handled as before.

Reproduction: a root directory with a record whose byte 1 is 0x80,
followed by SYSTEM.CNF;1, fed to host builds of both copies of
cdvdman_locatefile(). Before: AddressSanitizer reports a read before
cdvdman_buf. After: SYSTEM.CNF;1 is found.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zso: reject headers with align above 11

read_raw_data() computes the sector of a ZSO block as
offset / (2048 >> align). Every copy of it (isofs, the EE frontend and
the in-game CDVDMAN) divides by zero when the header's align byte is
above 11, and a shift of 32 or more is undefined in C. Nothing checked
the byte: ziso.py writes align = total size / 2^31, so real images
use 0 to 3.

ziso_init() now returns -1 for such a header, and its callers treat the
file as not being a ZSO image. The game list (isofs) then does not find
an ISO9660 volume in it and skips the file; launching it no longer
divides by zero.

Reproduction: a ZSO header with align = 12 passed to host builds of
ziso_init() and isofs read_raw_data(). Before: the first index read
fails with an integer divide by zero. After: ziso_init() returns -1.
Align 0 and 11 read as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ps2cnf: reject a BOOT2 line without '='

CNFGetToken() returns NULL when the text does not match the token. The
result of the "=" lookup was only compared with -1, so for a line such
as "BOOT2 cdrom0:\SLUS_200.62;1" ps2cnfGetBootFile() passed NULL to
CNFGetKey(), which dereferences it. This runs for every ISO the game
list has not cached yet (GetStartupExecName() in supportbase.c).

Treat a missing '=' like the other parse failures: the image has no
usable boot file and is skipped.

The same check is in RiptOPL's C++ edition
(NathanNeurotic/RiptOPL@a9cf8088, src/platform/ps2cnf.cpp).

Reproduction: a SYSTEM.CNF with "BOOT2 cdrom0:\SLUS_200.62;1" passed to
a host build of ps2cnfGetBootFile(). Before: access violation at
address 0 in CNFGetKey(). After: it returns -1. "BOOT2 = ..." parses as
before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

supportbase: ignore a partial record at the end of ul.cfg

sbReadList() sizes the game list for size / 64 ul.cfg records, but
read records while size > 0. When the file size is not a multiple of
64, the last iteration read a partial record over the previous one and
stored it in one slot more than the list had room for:
- with no ISO games, that write went past the end of the list;
- with ISO games, the garbage entry took the place of the last ISO
  game, which was dropped from the list.

Read whole records only.

RiptOPL's C++ edition reads records the same way
(NathanNeurotic/RiptOPL@65ea056d, src/sources/supportbase.cpp).

Reproduction: host build of sbReadList() over a ul.cfg of one record
plus one byte.
- No ISO games. Before: AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow
  write; a plain build corrupts the heap. After: one game.
- Two ISO games. Before: "Game A", an empty entry, "Game 0"; "Game 1"
  is missing. After: "Game A", "Game 0", "Game 1".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

supportbase: look up each listed game in the whole games.bin cache

updateISOGameList() decides whether games.bin must be rewritten. Its
inner loop runs j over the cached entries but compared
cache->games[i], the entry at the position of the listed game, every
time. So:
- when the folder has more games than the cache, cache->games[i] is
  read past the end of the cache array;
- the same games in another order counted as a change, because only
  the entry at the same position could ever match.

Compare with cache->games[j], as the loop intends. A folder whose games
are all in the cache, in any order, keeps its games.bin; an added or
removed game still rewrites it.

RiptOPL removed the out-of-bounds read with a position-by-position
comparison instead (NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@515c534a), which
keeps rewriting the cache when the order changes.

Reproduction: host build of updateISOGameList().
- Cache of 1 game, folder of 2. Before: AddressSanitizer reports a
  heap-buffer-overflow read. After: games.bin is rewritten.
- Same 3 games, first two swapped. Before: rewritten. After: kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

system: hash ul.cfg names as unsigned bytes in USBA_crc32()

USBA_crc32() gives the CRC in the ul.%08X.<ID>.%02x chunk names of
ul.cfg games. It read each name byte through a plain char, which is
signed on the EE. A byte of 0x80 or more (a non-ASCII title, e.g.
Cyrillic or Japanese) became negative, and crctab[byte ^ ...] read
memory before crctab. The CRC of such a title therefore depended on
whatever the build placed before the table, so OPL looked for chunk
files that no PC tool had written.

Read the bytes as unsigned char. ASCII titles keep their CRC. For other
titles the CRC is now the one that tools hashing unsigned bytes compute
(PyOPLM, YAOPLM; RiptOPL made the same change in
NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@eb277b61). A non-ASCII ul game whose
chunks happen to carry the old, build-specific CRC will need its chunks
renamed.

Reproduction: host build of USBA_crc32() (MSVC char is signed, as on
the EE). "A" -> 935FAD90 and "Grand Theft Auto III" -> 10D00014 before
and after. CP1251 "Игра" (C8 E3 F0 E0): before, 00000000 in a plain
build and AA71C331 in an AddressSanitizer build of the same code;
after, E857E311 in both. 300 random names with bytes 01-FF match an
independent unsigned implementation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

pc: hash names as unsigned bytes in iso2opl and opl2iso

Both tools carry a copy of USBA_crc32() that reads the name through a
plain char. On x86 that char is signed, so a non-ASCII game name gave
a negative table index and a CRC that depends on the build, as in OPL
before the previous commit. Read the bytes as unsigned char so both
tools name ul chunks the way OPL now looks them up.

Reproduction: host build of iso2opl's crc32(). CP1251 "Игра" now gives
E857E311, the same as OPL's USBA_crc32(); ASCII names are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

supportbase: check the name length before looking at its extension

isValidIsoName() compares &name[size - 4] with ".iso" before checking
the length. For a name shorter than 4 bytes, such as the "." and ".."
entries that readdir() returns in every CD and DVD subfolder, that
pointer is before the start of the name.

Return early for names shorter than 5 bytes ("x.iso"), which are not
images anyway.

RiptOPL has the same guard (NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@eb277b61).

Reproduction: host build of isValidIsoName() with "..". Before:
AddressSanitizer reports a read 2 bytes before the name. After: it
returns 0 without reading outside the name. Image names give the same
results as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

isofs, cdvdman: bound the file name copy in cdvdman_findfile()

cdvdman_findfile() fills the 16-byte name field of the result with
strcpy(name, strrchr(path, '\') + 1). Two problems:
- The game list opens "iso:/SYSTEM.CNF;1", so isofs gets
  "/SYSTEM.CNF;1". It has no '\', strrchr() returns NULL, and strcpy()
  copies from address 1 of IOP memory into the name, for every image
  that is not in games.bin yet.
- A name of 16 characters or more, possible with ISO 9660 level 2
  names, runs past the field into the rest of the result and the stack.

Take the last component after '\' or '/' (the whole path if there is
neither) and cut it to fit. The name is informational: callers use the
LSN and size. The in-game copy in searchfile.c (sceCdSearchFile) gets
the same change.

RiptOPL bounds the isofs copy in
NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@03f50fa6.

Reproduction: host build of the isofs cdvdman_findfile() on a fake
root directory.
- "/SYSTEM.CNF;1". Before: access violation at address 1 in strcpy().
  After: found, name "SYSTEM.CNF;1".
- "\A_VERY_LONG_LEVEL2_FILENAME.TXT;1". Before: AddressSanitizer
  reports a stack-buffer-overflow. After: name "A_VERY_LONG_LEV".
- "\SYSTEM.CNF;1" gives the same result as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cdvdman: do not overflow cdvdman_curdir on long directory entry names

The in-game cdvdman_locatefile() copies the name of every directory
record it walks past into char cdvdman_curdir[15], using the record's
own name length (up to 255). A file or folder name longer than 14
characters, which ISO 9660 level 2 allows and which rebuilt images can
contain, overwrites the IOP stack whenever the game looks up any file
in that directory.

Cut the copy to the buffer. Names are compared on 12 characters only,
so lookups give the same results.

Reproduction: host build of the in-game cdvdman_locatefile() on a root
directory holding a 33-character name before SYSTEM.CNF;1. Before:
AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow in strncpy(). After:
SYSTEM.CNF;1 is found with no report.

vmc: find the mcemu slot words even after an aborted launch

The BDM, SMB and HDD launch code finds VMC slot N in the embedded mcemu
image by its marker word 0xC0DEFAC0 + N and overwrites it with the
slot's settings. Nothing restores the marker, and a launch can still
return to the menu afterwards (a declined VMC prompt, an invalid or too
fragmented image). The next launch then:
- did not find the marker, and scanned on with a word index bounded by
  the image size in bytes, i.e. up to 4 times past the image, possibly
  into the next mcemu image, where it found that image's marker and
  wrote the slot there;
- loaded mcemu with the slots of the aborted launch: the game ran
  without its VMC, or with the previous game's VMC;
- on HDD, also kept a slot that it does not use active, since HDD wrote
  only the slots that have a VMC.

sbMcemuSlotWord() looks each marker up once, while the image is still
pristine, within size / 4 words, and remembers it. HDD now writes both
slots, inactive when unused.

RiptOPL fixed this with a similar helper
(NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader@afa0ab42).

a name that does not exist; launch A and answer "No" at the slot 2
error. Then launch game B with VMC slot 1 = "B" and save in game.
Before: B saves to the physical card or to A.bin. After: B.bin changes.

one table of BDM_MAX_FRAGS (64) entries. For each part it passes the
room left, but checked the result against the whole table. ps2sdk's

bdm: allocate the device data again after the NBD server

Starting the NBD server runs deinitAllSupport(), and bdmCleanUp() frees
each BDM device's data and sets priv to NULL while the device stays
"enabled". When the server stops, initAllSupport(1) reaches
bdmInitDevicesData(), which only allocates the data on its first call:
in Auto start mode it then wrote bdmDeviceTick through the NULL pointer
(and later code read through it too). OPL crashes or freezes when it
returns from the NBD server with BDM in Auto mode, or in Manual mode
once BDM was started.

initialized, so it is set up as on the first start. bdmCleanUp() and
bdmShutdown() also skip data that is already gone.

Problem: ziso_read_sector() trusts the block index of the image. The
size of the compressed data is (o_end - o_start) << align with no check
against the count * 2048 bytes the caller provides, and the data is read
to the end of that buffer: an index whose end offset lies before its
start offset (a corrupt or truncated .zso, or a download gone wrong)
gives a huge size, and read_raw_data() writes the file in front of the
buffer. The EE reads the image into the 2 KiB IOBuffer for the game
list and the launch, the game reads into the IOP's buffers.

mmce: build switch for the console A/B of the in-game SIO2MAN

Problem: the central risk of MMCE support is the pairing of the in-game
driver with the SIO2MAN module. OPL packs the SDK sio2man into every game
since upstream #1785, and the mmceman modules of 2026-06 (cccc366) hook
only that sio2man; RiptOPL reports instead that its stock 2025 driver
black-screens after the PS2 logo with the SDK sio2man loaded first and
skips it for MMCE games (11a5150e). Nobody has reported the pairing this
fork ships (modules of 2026-08 plus the SDK sio2man) on hardware.

Fix: keep upstream's module set as the default and make the alternative a
build switch: make MMCE_NO_SDK_SIO2MAN=1 leaves the SDK sio2man and mcemu
out of MMCE games (they keep the game's own SIO2MAN, VMC and PADEMU would
hook it) and marks the version with -nosio2man. The CI-compile workflow
takes extra make arguments on a manual run, so both builds come from the
same commit for the console A/B.

Origin: RiptOPL 11a5150e for the alternative; the decision is in the kb
plan (variant (b) first, (a) for the A/B).

Before/after: a push build is unchanged (the switch is off). The console
decides: if the default build black-screens after the PS2 logo on an MMCE
game, the -nosio2man build of the same commit is the comparison.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

mmce: send the game ID to the MMCE card after the last memory-card write

Problem: an MMCE card keeps one virtual memory card per game and switches
to it when told which game starts. The ps2-mmce fork sends the ID only
for games on the card, before deinit(), and then OPL still writes the OSD
history record to mc0: inside sysLaunchLoaderElf(): that write lands on
the game's card instead of the boot card. It also waits up to 15 x 1 s.

Fix: mmceSendGameID() runs from sysLaunchLoaderElf() right after the OSD
history record, so every memory-card write of the launch (last played,
per-game settings, history) precedes the switch, and for games on every
device (USB, MX4SIO, MMCE): the boot file name without path and version
goes to each port that answered a ping (pinged once per session), with
wOPL's bounded wait (200 ms, then up to 20 x 100 ms polling the busy bit).
Setting "Send the game ID to the card" (mmce_gameid, default on) in the
MMCE settings; mmceman is loaded for it when the MMCE device is off.

Origin: ps2-mmce/Open-PS2-Loader 949c734 and 97acabd (devctl 0x8 and the
busy poll); wOPL dca04cf (bound and all devices); the order relative to
the history record is this fork's.

Before/after: console only. Before: the card does not switch for USB and
MX4SIO games, and for MMCE games the OSD history of the launch goes to the
game's card. After: the card shows the game's card from the launch on,
and the boot card keeps the history and settings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

mmce: IGR switches back the card(s) that answered, not both slots by default

Problem: the ps2-mmce fork defaults the IGR setting to "both slots", so on
every IGR the single-shot mmceigr module sends raw MMCE commands to both
memory-card ports. With an MX4SIO in the other slot that is a transfer
that times out on each IGR, and the module is packed into kernel RAM for
every game whether or not an MMCE card is present.

Fix: a new value "Auto" of the IGR slot setting, the default: the slots
to switch are the ones where an MMCE card answered the ping (probed once
per session), mmceIGRSlots(). mmceigr is packed and MMCEIGRSettings set
only when that is not empty; the explicit values 1, 2 and Both still work
as before.

Origin: the mechanism is the fork's (d4160d4); the default is this fork's,
after the MX4SIO sharing note in the kb plan.

Before/after: console only. Before: IGR with an MX4SIO in slot 2 waits
for a timed-out transfer on port 3; after: only the card's slot is
addressed. The user's PSXMemCard Gen2 sits in slot 1, the MX4SIO in slot 2.

+# CLAUDE.md — YAOPL agent rules
+
+YAOPL (Yet Another Open PS2 Loader) is our fork of Open PS2 Loader that we develop ourselves. Users install the
+ELF that CI publishes from `master`. Its PC-side companion is YAOPLM (Yet Another OPL Manager), a separate project.
+
+Read before working: `FORK.md` (what differs from upstream and why), `README.md` (header), `CONTRIBUTING.md`
+(upstream's code rules), `labs/host-repro/README.md`. If the local knowledge base `kb/` exists, start with
+`kb/README.md` and `kb/ROADMAP.md`.
+
+## Knowledge base
+- `kb/` is local only: it is listed in `.git/info/exclude` and must never be committed or pushed, to our GitHub or
+  upstream. Do not `git add -f` it.
+- Keep it current: `ROADMAP.md` (what is next), `DECISIONS.md` (new decisions as ADRs), `HISTORY.md` (major steps),
+  `TESTING.md`, and `research/` for findings. Core docs are in Russian, `research/` in English.
+
+## Communication
+- Talk to the user in **Russian**. They own the project and test on a real PS2.
+- Write code, comments, commit messages and public docs in **English**.
+- After a set of fixes, give the user a short Russian checklist of what to test on the console.
+
+## Rules
+1. **Licence.** YAOPL is AFL-3.0 like OPL. Never copy code from YAOPLM (GPL-3.0) into YAOPL, or the other way.
+2. **`master` is the release.** Every push to `master` publishes the public `latest` pre-release. Push only
+   finished, checked work. Prepare bigger changes on a short-lived branch and delete it after the merge.
+   Only the build of master's tip is published: a commit that does not change the ELF (`labs/`, docs) may say
+   `[skip ci]`, but push it only after the running build has published, or that build is not released.
+3. **Keep `FORK.md` current.** Every fix or behaviour change updates the table in `FORK.md` (area, fix, origin)
+   in the same push. Update the README header if what YAOPL is or how to get it changes.
+4. **One fix per commit.** Subject `<component>: <summary>`. The body states the problem, the fix, its origin
+   (credit the RiptOPL commit for ported fixes) and the reproduction with the result before and after.
+5. **Check every fix** (details in `FORK.md`, "How fixes are checked"):
+   - reproduce on an upstream tree first (`labs/host-repro/run_all.ps1 -Opl <tree>`, or a console test);
+   - rerun the same check after the fix, then all checks for regressions;
+   - format with clang-format 12 (`make format`, or the `clang-format` 12.0.1 Python wheel on Windows);
+   - the GitHub Actions build must pass; then the user tests on the console.
+   Host checks do not emulate the PS2. Say so when a fix is only checked on the host or only by reading code.
+6. **RiptOPL and other forks are sources of candidates, not truth.** Check each change against upstream code:
+   take real bugs and zero-risk hardening, in the smallest form; skip speculative or behaviour-changing ones.
+7. **Small, upstream-shaped diffs**, so merging upstream stays easy. Fix GCC warnings.
+8. **Upstream contributions** (issues, PRs to ps2homebrew) only when the user asks.
+9. **Repository settings** (Actions, Pages, branch rules, releases) and anything posted publicly: ask first.
+10. **User data and devices.** Never write to the user's removable drives without a plan and an explicit OK.
+    Test data lives in `D:\yaoplm-testdata\` (reference clones in `refs\`, console test files in
+    `opl-fork-tests\`); write on D: only there.
+
+## Commands
+- Host checks: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File labs\host-repro\run_all.ps1 [-Opl <tree>] [-Only cheat,cfg,...] [-Images <dir of .iso>]`
+- Console test files: `python labs/host-repro/make_console_kit.py <bootable.iso> <out dir>`
+- CI: `gh run list -R belomaxorka/yaopl`, `gh workflow run compilation.yml -R belomaxorka/yaopl --ref master`
+- Upstream sync: see `FORK.md`, "Pulling in upstream changes".

+# YAOPL and upstream OPL
+
+YAOPL (Yet Another Open PS2 Loader) is a fork of [Open PS2 Loader](https://github.com/ps2homebrew/Open-PS2-Loader)
+that continues its development. It follows upstream and adds fixes for crashes, hangs, memory errors and data
+loss that OPL hits on malformed or unusual files: cheat files, ISO and ZSO images, `SYSTEM.CNF`, `ul.cfg`,
+`games.bin`, configuration files and VMCs. It is not an official OPL build. The licence is the same as
+upstream's (AFL-3.0, see `LICENSE`).
+
+## Getting a build
+
+Every push to `master` builds OPL in GitHub Actions and replaces the `latest` pre-release of this
+repository: the ELF (`OPNPS2LD.ELF`), the upstream-style 7z packages and `SHA256SUMS`. Check a
+download with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` (Linux) or compare `Get-FileHash <file>` (Windows).
+Only the build of the current tip of `master` is published.
+
+YAOPL builds carry the suffix `-yaopl` in their version string (`LOCALVERSION` in the `Makefile`),
+for example `v1.2.0-Beta-2310-1a2b3c4-yaopl`. The revision number counts this fork's commits, so it
+does not match upstream's numbering.
+
+## What differs from upstream
+
+| Area | Fix | Origin |
+|---|---|---|
+| Cheats | A comment line with leading blanks no longer becomes a cheat with an empty name | this fork |
+| Cheats | The 251st cheat is no longer written past the cheat table | this fork; overflow found by RiptOPL |
+| Cheats | `make_code()` no longer writes one byte past `digits[]` for every code | RiptOPL |
+| Cheats | A last line without LF is no longer read past the end of the buffer or copied past `line[]` | RiptOPL |
+| Cheats | Remembered picks of cheats that share a name survive a reload | RiptOPL |
+| ISO | A directory record with an empty name no longer hangs the game list or the game | this fork |
+| ISO | The record length is read as one byte; an extended attribute length no longer derails the scan | this fork |
+| ISO | In-game lookups no longer overflow `cdvdman_curdir[15]` on names longer than 14 characters | this fork |
+| ISO | `cdvdman_findfile()` no longer copies from address 1 or past the 16-byte name | RiptOPL (isofs), this fork (in-game) |
+| ZSO | A header with `align` above 11 is rejected instead of dividing by zero | this fork |
+| In-game | 2340-byte sector reads no longer write past the game's buffer | RiptOPL |
+| `SYSTEM.CNF` | `BOOT2` without `=` no longer passes NULL to the parser | RiptOPL C++ edition |
+| `ul.cfg` | A partial record at the end is ignored instead of written past the game list | RiptOPL C++ edition |
+| `ul.cfg` | `USBA_crc32()` hashes names as unsigned bytes (non-ASCII titles), also in `pc/` tools | RiptOPL |
+| `games.bin` | Each listed game is looked up in the whole cache, without reading past it | this fork |
+| Game list | `isValidIsoName()` no longer reads before short names such as `..` | RiptOPL |
+| Config files | A CFG, theme or language file whose last line is a `#` comment without LF no longer crashes OPL | this fork |
+| Config files | A read error (device removed) ends the file instead of corrupting memory | RiptOPL |
+| Config files | Keys of 32+ and values of 256+ characters are cut and terminated | RiptOPL |
+| Config files | A long line without `=` no longer overflows the prefix buffer | RiptOPL |
+| Settings | A failed save (e.g. full memory card) is reported instead of "Settings saved" | RiptOPL |
+| Settings | Looking for a USB device to save to no longer empties its `conf_opl.cfg` (upstream issue #1397) | this fork; RiptOPL has the same change |
+| Themes | A colour with more than three bytes (`#RRGGBBAA`) no longer writes past the colour | RiptOPL |
+| Network | An `IPCONFIG.DAT` of 256 bytes or more no longer overflows the stack | RiptOPL |
+| VMC | Leaving the VMC menu no longer replaces a card of another size (4 MB, 128 MB, PCSX2 `.ps2`); Modify asks first | this fork, after RiptOPL |

+| BDM | All parts of a UL game must fit the fragment table together | RiptOPL |
+| BDM | One VMC error is no longer reported again for the other slot | RiptOPL |
+| BDM | Returning from the NBD server no longer crashes | RiptOPL |
+| HDD | The PS2 logo check reads 48 sectors, not 49 | RiptOPL |
+| Misc | Format string, terminators and the IOP patch mode compare (hardening, no known trigger) | RiptOPL |
+| Cheats | A code line with address 0 (the second half of a multi-line code) no longer ends the cheat (upstream issue #1548) | this fork |
+| Cheats | More than 5 hooks or 250 codes are dropped instead of written past the engine's tables (`SLUS_210.09.cht` has 9 hooks) | this fork |
+| Themes | `fntFitString()` stops at the end of the string instead of scanning and writing past it (upstream issue #1713) | this fork |
+| Themes | Wrapped text is a private copy: line breaks no longer go into the game's CFG (upstream issue #1713) | RiptOPL (same fix) |
+| Themes | `GameCountText` gets the 60 bytes it formats into, not 1 | this fork; RiptOPL has the same fix |
+| Themes | An image file that is missing disables the element instead of leaving a garbage texture that is drawn and freed | this fork; RiptOPL has the same fix |
+| Themes | A theme without an `ItemsList` keeps the default list, instead of a NULL that crashes the first scroll | this fork; RiptOPL has the same fix |
+| Languages | A `.lng` file name shorter than `lang_X.lng` (for example `ru.lng`) no longer crashes OPL at boot | this fork; RiptOPL checks the prefix |
+| Launch | A boot file name over 16 characters (`$AltStartup`) no longer overflows the OSD history buffer | this fork |
+| Settings | The default BGM path is no longer used as a format string | this fork |
+| GSM | A `$GSMVMode` outside the table of modes falls back to mode 0 instead of reading past the table | RiptOPL |
+| Pad | A held button keeps repeating across the 29 s wrap of the tick counter | RiptOPL (upstream PR #1757) |
+| VMC | A failed cluster write while creating a VMC no longer leaves genvmc's abort semaphore taken (the next creation hung) | RiptOPL, smaller form |
+| GUI | The scroll speed is restored after dialogs that return through their updater (VMC menu) | upstream PR #1757 |
+| Art | Grey and grey+alpha PNGs are loaded | wOPL |
+| ZSO | Images with a block size other than 2048 (maxcso default for 2 GiB+ images: 16 KiB) are rejected instead of read as the wrong sectors | this fork |
+| ZSO | The block index is checked before the compressed data is read: a corrupt index gives a read error, not a write before the buffer | this fork |
+| ZSO | Reads of more than 256 sectors go in slices instead of running past the index cache | this fork |
+| In-game | IGR is sampled from the VBLANK_END interrupt handler again, not by a polling thread that busy games starve (upstream issue #1787); Fatal Fury: Battle Archives Vol. 2 needs Mode 6 as before | revert of upstream PR #1762, as RiptOPL 38481e9c |
+| USB | `usbd_mini` is built from the ps2sdk USBD sources from before the "USBD feature update" (ps2sdk b1f7ff96, OPL Beta-2127): with the rewritten USBD, Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex takes minutes to load from USB and then black-screens (upstream issue #1751, ps2sdk issue #908). `download_usbd.sh` fetches the sources, `modules/usb/usbd_mini` builds them; drop both once ps2sdk fixes its USBD | upstream PR #1752 (prebuilt binaries), ps2sdk PR #911 |
+| MMCE | A new device, MMCE (Settings → MMCE Settings): games in `CD` and `DVD` on an MMCE memory-card emulator (SD2PSX, MemCard PRO 2, PSXMemCard Gen2) are listed and started, the ISO streamed in game by `mmcedrv` over SIO2; IGR switches the card back to its boot card. Not yet: VMCs on the card, games split into parts. The modules `mmceman`, `mmcedrv` and `mmceigr` are built from `ps2-mmce/mmceman` (MIT, see `CREDITS`) by `download_mmce.sh`. MMCE games get the SDK `sio2man` like every other game; `make MMCE_NO_SDK_SIO2MAN=1` builds the alternative (RiptOPL's: the game's own SIO2MAN) for a console A/B, with `-nosio2man` in the version | ps2-mmce/Open-PS2-Loader `mmce_support` (qnox32, BBsan), hardening after RiptOPL 09618a06, b5df7836 |
+
+RiptOPL is [NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader](https://github.com/NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader) and its C++ edition
+[NathanNeurotic/RiptOPL](https://github.com/NathanNeurotic/RiptOPL). Its fixes were reviewed one by one against
+upstream: only those that fix a defect present in upstream were taken, some in a smaller or corrected form. Each
+commit credits the RiptOPL commit it ports.
+
+**Compatibility note:** a `ul.cfg` game whose title has non-ASCII bytes now uses the CRC that PC tools
+compute. Upstream's CRC for such titles depended on the build, so chunks named by upstream OPL itself
+may need renaming.
+
+## How fixes are checked
+
+Each fix is a separate commit whose message states the problem, the fix, its origin and the reproduction.
+
+1. Reproduce the bug on an upstream tree, with a host check (`labs/host-repro/run_all.ps1 -Opl <tree>`) or,
+   for code that only runs on the console, a console test.
+2. Fix it, then rerun the same check on this tree: the bug must be gone.
+3. Rerun all host checks, and the real data where it applies (cheat corpus, ISO fixtures), for regressions.
+4. Format with clang-format 12, as `CI-format-check` does.
+5. The GitHub Actions build (ps2dev toolchain) must pass; then test on a console.
+
+`labs/host-repro/` holds the host checks. They compile OPL's own functions, taken from the tree at build
+time, on Windows with MSVC and AddressSanitizer, with stubs in place of PS2 I/O. They show logic errors and
+memory errors on the given inputs; they do not emulate the PS2, so a console test remains the final check.
+`make_console_kit.py` turns a bootable ISO into the malformed test files for a console.
+
+## Branches
+
+`master` is the only long-lived branch: the releases are built from it. A fix may be prepared on a
+short-lived branch, which is deleted once it is merged into `master`.
+
+The branches `copilot/*`, `main`, `master_old` and `v1.1.z` came from upstream when the fork was
+created; this fork does not use them. Upstream's website branch `gh-pages` was deleted and GitHub Pages
+is off, so no copy of the official OPL site is published here.
+
+## Pulling in upstream changes
+
+```
+git remote add upstream https://github.com/ps2homebrew/Open-PS2-Loader.git   # once
+git fetch upstream
+git switch master
+git merge upstream/master        # resolve conflicts, keeping this fork's fixes
+git push origin master           # CI builds and publishes the new pre-release
+```
+
+Do not use GitHub's "Sync fork" button with "Discard commits": it would drop this fork's fixes.
+Before pushing a merge, run `labs/host-repro/run_all.ps1` if upstream touched the files it covers.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""List the IOP modules (IRX files) embedded in an unpacked OPL ELF: size, SHA-256, module version
+from .iopmod (the names are stripped) and the export table(s) if the module has any.
+Usage: elfmods.py <ELF> [<ELF2>]  (two files: compare them module by module, by position, then compare
+the bytes of the loadable segments that lie outside the modules)"""
+import hashlib
+import struct
+import sys
+
+
+def irx_modules(data):
+    mods = []
+    pos = 0
+    while True:
+        pos = data.find(b"\x7fELF", pos)
+        if pos < 0:
+            break
+        hdr = data[pos:pos + 52]
+        if len(hdr) < 52 or hdr[4] != 1 or hdr[5] != 1:
+            pos += 4
+            continue
+        e_type = struct.unpack_from("<H", hdr, 16)[0]
+        if e_type != 0xFF80:  # ET_SCE_IOPRELEXEC
+            pos += 4
+            continue
+        (e_phoff, e_shoff, _flags, _ehsize, e_phentsize, e_phnum,
+         e_shentsize, e_shnum, _shstrndx) = struct.unpack_from("<IIIHHHHHH", hdr, 28)
+        end = 52
+        if e_shoff and e_shnum:
+            end = max(end, e_shoff + e_shnum * e_shentsize)
+            for i in range(e_shnum):
+                sh = data[pos + e_shoff + i * e_shentsize:pos + e_shoff + (i + 1) * e_shentsize]
+                sh_type, _f, _a, sh_off, sh_size = struct.unpack_from("<IIIII", sh, 4)
+                if sh_type != 8:  # SHT_NOBITS
+                    end = max(end, sh_off + sh_size)
+        ver = "?"
+        for i in range(e_phnum):
+            ph = data[pos + e_phoff + i * e_phentsize:pos + e_phoff + (i + 1) * e_phentsize]
+            p_type, p_off, _v, _p, p_filesz = struct.unpack_from("<IIIII", ph, 0)
+            end = max(end, p_off + p_filesz)
+            if p_type == 0x70000080 and p_filesz >= 0x1A:  # .iopmod: ... u16 version at 0x18
+                v = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, pos + p_off + 0x18)[0]
+                ver = "%d.%d" % (v >> 8, v & 0xFF)
+        blob = data[pos:pos + end]
+        mods.append(dict(off=pos, size=end, sha=hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest(), ver=ver,
+                         exp=export_versions(blob)))
+        pos += end
+    return mods
+
+
+def export_versions(blob):
+    # irx_export_table: u32 magic 0x41C00000, u32 next, u16 version, u16 mode, char name[8]
+    found = []
+    pos = 0
+    while True:
+        pos = blob.find(b"\x00\x00\xC0\x41", pos)
+        if pos < 0:
+            break
+        if pos + 20 <= len(blob):
+            nxt, ver, _mode = struct.unpack_from("<IHH", blob, pos + 4)
+            raw = blob[pos + 12:pos + 20].split(b"\0", 1)[0]
+            if nxt == 0 and raw and all(32 <= c < 127 for c in raw):
+                found.append("%s %d.%d" % (raw.decode("ascii"), ver >> 8, ver & 0xFF))
+        pos += 4
+    return ", ".join(found)
+
+
+def load_segments(data):
+    """File ranges of the PT_LOAD segments of the (outer) ELF: what the console loads."""
+    e_phoff = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, 28)[0]
+    e_phentsize, e_phnum = struct.unpack_from("<HH", data, 42)
+    ranges = []
+    for i in range(e_phnum):
+        p_type, p_off, _v, _p, p_filesz = struct.unpack_from("<IIIII", data, e_phoff + i * e_phentsize)
+        if p_type == 1 and p_filesz:
+            ranges.append((p_off, p_off + p_filesz))
+    return ranges
+
+
+def show(path):
+    data = open(path, "rb").read()
+    mods = irx_modules(data)
+    segs = load_segments(data)
+    print("%s: %d bytes, %d bytes in %d loadable segments, %d IRX modules" % (
+        path, len(data), sum(b - a for a, b in segs), len(segs), len(mods)))
+    for i, m in enumerate(mods):
+        print("  #%02d v%-6s %7d bytes  exports: %-24s sha256 %s" % (i, m["ver"], m["size"], m["exp"] or "-", m["sha"][:16]))
+    return data, mods, segs
+
+
+def loaded_outside(data, mods, segs):
+    """The bytes of the loadable segments that are not part of an embedded module."""
+    out = bytearray()
+    for a, b in segs:
+        pos = a
+        for m in mods:
+            if m["off"] >= b or m["off"] + m["size"] <= a:
+                continue
+            out += data[pos:max(pos, m["off"])]
+            pos = max(pos, m["off"] + m["size"])
+        out += data[pos:b]
+    return bytes(out)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    data, mods, segs = show(sys.argv[1])
+    if len(sys.argv) > 2:
+        data2, mods2, segs2 = show(sys.argv[2])
+        print("")

+# Host reproductions of parser bugs
+
+Small host programs that run OPL's own functions on malformed input and report
+crashes, endless loops and AddressSanitizer findings. Each fix commit of this fork names
+the check that shows its bug, with the result before and after.
+
+Nothing here is built into OPL. The harnesses do not carry copies of OPL code:
+`extract.py` copies the functions under test out of the OPL tree at build time, so one run
+checks whatever is checked out.
+
+## Run
+
+Windows with Visual Studio Build Tools (MSVC with AddressSanitizer) and Python 3:
+
+```
+powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File labs\host-repro\run_all.ps1 [-Opl <OPL checkout>] [-Only <groups>] [-Images <dir>] [-Expected <file>]
+```
+
+`-Opl` defaults to this checkout. Inputs and binaries go to `labs/host-repro/build/`.
+MSVC's `char` is signed, as on the EE and the IOP. `-Only cheat,zso,...` runs some groups
+only. `-Images <dir>` also prints the game ID OPL derives from every `.iso` in the directory.
+
+`-Expected labs\host-repro\expected.txt` compares every result line with that file and
+exits with 1 on a difference. `CI-host-checks` (`.github/workflows/host-checks.yml`) runs
+the checks that way on `windows-latest` for every push. After adding or changing a check,
+regenerate the file from a run on this tree:
+`run_all.ps1 > labs\host-repro\expected.txt` (its first line, the tree path, is ignored).
+
+## What it covers
+

+|---|---|---|
+| `cheat` | `src/cheatman.c` `make_code()` | writes `digits[16]`, one byte past the array, for every code |
+| `cheat` | `parse_buf()`, `trim_str()` | an indented comment becomes a cheat named `" "` |
+| `cheat` | `parse_buf()` | the 251st cheat is written to `gCheats[250]` |
+| `cheat` | `parse_buf()` | a last line over 255 bytes without LF overflows `line[]` |
+| `cheat` | `parse_buf()` | a last line without LF reads past the buffer |
+| `cheat` | `set_cheats_list()` | a code line with address 0 ends the cheat (upstream #1548) |
+| `cheat` | `ee_core/src/cheat_api.c` `SetupCheats()` | more than 5 hooks or 250 codes overflow the engine's tables (`cheat-t -s <list>` sweeps a corpus) |
+| `iso` | `cdvdman_locatefile()`, isofs and in-game | a record with name length 0 loops forever; an extended attribute length >= 0x80 steps backwards; in-game, a name over 14 characters overflows `cdvdman_curdir[15]` |
+| `find` | `cdvdman_findfile()` | a `/`-only path copies from address 1; long names overflow `name[16]` |
+| `zso` | `ziso_init()`, `read_raw_data()` | align > 11 divides by zero; a block size other than 2048 is read as the wrong sectors |
+| `zso` | `ziso_read_sector()` with the tree's LZ4 | a corrupt index writes in front of the buffer; a read over 256 sectors runs past the index cache |
+| `cnf` | `ps2cnfGetBootFile()` | `BOOT2` without `=` passes NULL to `CNFGetKey()` |
+| `sb` | `sbReadList()`, `updateISOGameList()` | a ul.cfg size that is not a multiple of 64 writes past the list; the cache compare reads past the cache |

+| `cfg` | `readFileBuffer()`, `strToColor()`, `splitAssignment()`, `parsePrefix()`, `configReadLegacyIP()`, `CheckPS2Logo()` | a `#` last line without LF crashes; a read error corrupts memory; colours, keys, prefixes and `IPCONFIG.DAT` overflow; the HDD logo read is one sector too long |

+"""Copy named top-level C functions, #defines and structs out of an OPL source file.
+
+Usage: extract.py <source.c> <name> [<name> ...]
+A name matches a function definition (`... name(` at column 0, body up to the
+next `}` at column 0), a `#define name` (with its continuation lines), a
+`struct name` block or a `typedef struct { ... } name;` block. A name that
+starts with `?` may be absent (a helper that only a fixed tree has). Output
+goes to stdout in source order.
+"""
+import re
+import sys
+
+
+def main():
+    path = sys.argv[1]
+    required = set(n for n in sys.argv[2:] if not n.startswith("?"))
+    names = set(n.lstrip("?") for n in sys.argv[2:])
+    lines = open(path, encoding="latin-1").read().splitlines()
+    out, found = [], set()
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(lines):
+        line = lines[i]
+        m = re.match(r"#define\s+(\w+)", line)
+        if m and m.group(1) in names:
+            j = i
+            while lines[j].rstrip().endswith("\\"):
+                j += 1
+            out.extend(lines[i : j + 1])
+            found.add(m.group(1))
+            i = j + 1
+            continue
+        m = re.match(r"^struct\s+(\w+)\s*$", line)
+        if m and m.group(1) in names:
+            j = i
+            while not lines[j].startswith("}"):
+                j += 1
+            out.extend(lines[i : j + 1])
+            out.append("")
+            found.add(m.group(1))
+            i = j + 1
+            continue
+        if re.match(r"^typedef struct(\s+\w+)?\s*$", line):
+            j = i
+            while not lines[j].startswith("}"):
+                j += 1
+            m = re.match(r"^\}\s*(\w+)\s*;", lines[j])
+            if m and m.group(1) in names:
+                out.extend(lines[i : j + 1])
+                out.append("")
+                found.add(m.group(1))
+                i = j + 1
+                continue
+        m = re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_].*?\b(\w+)\s*\(", line)
+        if m and m.group(1) in names and not line.rstrip().endswith(";"):
+            j = i
+            while lines[j] != "}":
+                j += 1
+            out.extend(lines[i : j + 1])
+            out.append("")
+            found.add(m.group(1))
+            i = j + 1
+            continue
+        i += 1
+    missing = required - found
+    if missing:
+        sys.exit("not found in %s: %s" % (path, ", ".join(sorted(missing))))
+    print("\n".join(out))
+
+
+main()

+"""Build console test files for the parser fixes from one bootable PS2 ISO.
+
+Usage: make_console_kit.py <bootable.iso> <out dir>
+
+The ISO must have SYSTEM.CNF;1 in its root and fit its root directory in one sector, e.g. a
+homebrew ELF packed as a disc. Every variant keeps that ISO's game ID. Cheat files only use
+codes with address 0 and no hook line (9xxxxxxx): without a hook the cheat engine never
+applies the codes it is given.
+"""
+import os
+import shutil
+import struct
+import sys
+import zlib
+
+SECTOR = 2048
+
+
+def usba_crc32(name: bytes) -> int:
+    """USBA_crc32 with unsigned bytes, as OPL computes it after the fix."""
+    tab = [0] * 256
+    crc = 0
+    for t in range(256):
+        crc = (t << 24) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+        for _ in range(8):
+            crc = (crc << 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF if crc & 0x80000000 else ((crc << 1) ^ 0x04C11DB7) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+        tab[255 - t] = crc
+    for b in (name + b"\0")[:33]:
+        crc = tab[b ^ (crc >> 24)] ^ ((crc << 8) & 0xFFFFFF00)
+    return crc
+
+
+def root_dir(iso: bytearray):
+    pvd = 16 * SECTOR
+    assert iso[pvd] == 1 and iso[pvd + 1 : pvd + 6] == b"CD001"
+    lba, size = struct.unpack_from("<I", iso, pvd + 156 + 2)[0], struct.unpack_from("<I", iso, pvd + 156 + 10)[0]
+    assert size == SECTOR, "root directory must be one sector"
+    records, pos = [], lba * SECTOR
+    while iso[pos] != 0:
+        records.append(bytes(iso[pos : pos + iso[pos]]))
+        pos += iso[pos]
+    return lba, records
+
+
+def record(name: bytes, lba: int, size: int, xa: int = 0) -> bytes:
+    length = 33 + len(name) + (1 - len(name) % 2)  # ISO 9660 9.1.12: pad to an even length
+    r = bytearray(length)
+    r[0], r[1] = length, xa
+    struct.pack_into("<I", r, 2, lba)
+    struct.pack_into(">I", r, 6, lba)
+    struct.pack_into("<I", r, 10, size)
+    struct.pack_into(">I", r, 14, size)
+    r[32] = len(name)
+    r[33 : 33 + len(name)] = name
+    return bytes(r)
+
+
+def with_record_after_dotdot(base: bytes, extra: bytes) -> bytes:
+    """Insert a record right after '.' and '..', before SYSTEM.CNF;1, as OPL scans in order."""
+    iso = bytearray(base)
+    lba, records = root_dir(iso)
+    sector = b"".join(records[:2] + [extra] + records[2:])
+    assert len(sector) <= SECTOR
+    iso[lba * SECTOR : (lba + 1) * SECTOR] = sector.ljust(SECTOR, b"\0")
+    return bytes(iso)
+
+
+def system_cnf(iso: bytes):
+    _, records = root_dir(bytearray(iso))
+    for r in records:
+        if r[33 : 33 + r[32]] == b"SYSTEM.CNF;1":
+            return struct.unpack_from("<I", r, 2)[0], struct.unpack_from("<I", r, 10)[0]
+    raise SystemExit("no SYSTEM.CNF;1 in the root")
+
+
+def game_id(iso: bytes) -> bytes:
+    lba, size = system_cnf(iso)
+    cnf = iso[lba * SECTOR : lba * SECTOR + size]
+    value = cnf.split(b"BOOT2", 1)[1].split(b"=", 1)[1].strip().split(b"\r")[0].split(b"\n")[0]
+    return value.split(b":", 1)[1].lstrip(b"\\").split(b";")[0]
+
+
+def zso(iso: bytes, align: int = 0) -> bytes:
+    """ZSO with every block stored uncompressed (index bit 31 set)."""
+    blocks = len(iso) // SECTOR
+    data = 24 + 4 * (blocks + 1)
+    index = [((data + k * SECTOR) >> align) | 0x80000000 for k in range(blocks)] + [(data + blocks * SECTOR) >> align]
+    header = b"ZISO" + struct.pack("<IQIBB2x", 24, len(iso), SECTOR, 1, align)
+    return header + struct.pack("<%dI" % len(index), *index) + iso
+
+
+def zso_blocks(iso: bytes, block_size: int) -> bytes:
+    """ZSO with uncompressed blocks of block_size bytes, as maxcso writes 16 KiB blocks by default
+    for images of 2 GiB and more. The image is padded to whole blocks."""
+    iso = iso + b"\0" * ((-len(iso)) % block_size)
+    blocks = len(iso) // block_size
+    data = 24 + 4 * (blocks + 1)
+    index = [(data + k * block_size) | 0x80000000 for k in range(blocks)] + [data + blocks * block_size]
+    header = b"ZISO" + struct.pack("<IQIBB2x", 24, len(iso), block_size, 1, 0)
+    return header + struct.pack("<%dI" % len(index), *index) + iso
+
+
+def zso_bad_index(z: bytes, sector: int) -> bytes:
+    """Swap the index entries of `sector` and the next one: the sector then ends before it starts."""
+    z = bytearray(z)
+    a, b = 24 + 4 * sector, 24 + 4 * (sector + 1)
+    z[a : a + 4], z[b : b + 4] = z[b : b + 4], z[a : a + 4]
+    return bytes(z)
+
+
+def png_grey(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
+    """An 8-bit greyscale PNG (colour type 0) with a diagonal gradient."""
+
+    def chunk(tag: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
+        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
+
+    rows = b"".join(b"\0" + bytes((x + y) & 0xFF for x in range(width)) for y in range(height))
+    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0)
+    return b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(rows)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")
+
+

+main4:

+main5:

+\taligned=1
+\tx=POS_MID
+"""
+
+
+def ul_record(name: bytes, startup: bytes) -> bytes:
+    r = bytearray(64)
+    r[0 : len(name)] = name
+    r[0x20:0x23] = b"ul."
+    r[0x23 : 0x23 + len(startup)] = startup
+    r[0x2F] = 1  # parts
+    r[0x30] = 0x14  # DVD
+    r[0x35] = 0x08
+    return bytes(r)
+
+
+def write(path, data):
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+    with open(path, "wb") as f:
+        f.write(data)
+
+
+def main():
+    base = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
+    out = sys.argv[2]
+    gid = game_id(base)
+    cnf_lba, cnf_size = system_cnf(base)
+    dvd = os.path.join(out, "stick", "DVD")
+
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T0 control.iso"), base)
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T1 zero-length name.iso"), with_record_after_dotdot(base, record(b"", cnf_lba, cnf_size)))
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T2 ext-attr byte.iso"), with_record_after_dotdot(base, record(b"XA.TXT;1", cnf_lba, cnf_size, xa=0x80)))
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T3 long file name.iso"), with_record_after_dotdot(base, record(b"A_VERY_LONG_LEVEL2_FILENAME.TXT;1", cnf_lba, cnf_size)))
+    no_eq = bytearray(base)
+    start = cnf_lba * SECTOR
+    cnf = bytes(no_eq[start : start + cnf_size])
+    i = cnf.index(b"BOOT2") + 5
+    j = cnf.index(b"=", i)
+    no_eq[start + j] = ord(" ")
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T4 BOOT2 without equals.iso"), bytes(no_eq))
+    control_zso = zso(base, 0)
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T5 control.zso"), control_zso)
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T6 align 12.zso"), control_zso[:21] + bytes([12]) + control_zso[22:])
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T10 16k blocks.zso"), zso_blocks(base, 16384))
+    # The index of the SYSTEM.CNF sector is corrupt: reading it must fail, not write before the buffer
+    write(os.path.join(dvd, "T11 bad index.zso"), zso_bad_index(control_zso, cnf_lba))
+
+    # One record plus one stray byte; the chunk is the control image.
+    name = b"T7 ragged ul.cfg"
+    write(os.path.join(out, "ul-ragged", "ul.cfg"), ul_record(name, gid) + b"\0")
+    write(os.path.join(out, "ul-ragged", "ul.%08X.%s.00" % (usba_crc32(name), gid.decode())), base)
+
+    for name in (b"T8 ul ASCII title", "T9 Тест кириллицы".encode("utf-8")):
+        assert len(name) <= 32
+        write(os.path.join(out, "ul-cyrillic", "ul.%08X.%s.00" % (usba_crc32(name), gid.decode())), base)
+    write(
+        os.path.join(out, "ul-cyrillic", "ul.cfg"),
+        ul_record(b"T8 ul ASCII title", gid) + ul_record("T9 Тест кириллицы".encode("utf-8"), gid),
+    )
+
+    cht = gid.decode() + ".cht"
+    write(
+        os.path.join(out, "cht-indented", cht),
+        b'"Indented comment test"\r\nMastercode\r\n00000000 00000001\r\n\r\n'
+        b" //An indented comment\r\n00000000 00000002\r\n\r\nCheat B\r\n00000000 00000003\r\n",
+    )
+    write(os.path.join(out, "cht-251", cht), b"".join(b"Cheat %d\r\n00000000 %08X\r\n" % (n, n + 1) for n in range(251)))
+    write(os.path.join(out, "cht-long-last-line", cht), b"Cheat A\r\n00000000 00000001\r\nCheat B\r\n00000000 00000002\r\n" + b"X" * 400)
+    cht_dup = (
+        b"Mastercode\r\n00000000 00000001\r\n"
+        b"Character A\r\nInfinite Health\r\n00000000 00000002\r\n"
+        b"Character B\r\nInfinite Health\r\n00000000 00000003\r\n"
+    )
+    write(os.path.join(out, "cht-duplicate-names", cht), cht_dup)

+    nblocks = sectors * 2048 // block_size
+    unit = 1 << align
+    blocks = []
+    for b in range(nblocks):
+        data = b"".join(bytes([sector_byte(s)]) * 2048 for s in range(b * per_block, (b + 1) * per_block))
+        if raw_all or b % 2:
+            blocks.append((True, data))
+        else:
+            blocks.append((False, lz4_run(sector_byte(b), 2048)))
+    first = 24 + 4 * (nblocks + 1)
+    pos = (first + unit - 1) // unit * unit
+    index, body = [], b""
+    for raw, data in blocks:
+        index.append((pos // unit) | (0x80000000 if raw else 0))
+        padded = data + b"\0" * ((-len(data)) % unit)
+        body += padded
+        pos += len(padded)
+    index.append(pos // unit)
+    if swap:
+        index[swap[0]], index[swap[1]] = index[swap[1]], index[swap[0]]
+    header = struct.pack("<IIQIBBBB", 0x4F53495A, 24, sectors * 2048, block_size, 1, align, 0, 0)
+    with open(path, "wb") as f:
+        f.write(header + struct.pack("<%dI" % len(index), *index) + b"\0" * ((-first) % unit) + body)
+
+
+def zso_images(out):
+    zso_file(os.path.join(out, "zso_ok.zso"), 400)
+    zso_file(os.path.join(out, "zso_align4.zso"), 40, align=4)
+    zso_file(os.path.join(out, "zso_badidx.zso"), 10, swap=(3, 4))
+    # maxcso writes 16 KiB blocks by default for images of 2 GiB and more
+    zso_file(os.path.join(out, "zso_16k.zso"), 64, block_size=16384, raw_all=True)
+

+def main():

+    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
+    cheats(out)
+    ul_cfg(out)
+    system_cnf(out)
+    config_files(out)
+    zso_images(out)

+        f.write(bytes(65536))

+
+

+"""Independent USBA_crc32 with unsigned bytes (the behaviour the fix should give)."""
+import sys
+
+
+def usba_crc32(name: bytes) -> int:
+    tab = [0] * 256
+    crc = 0
+    for t in range(256):
+        crc = (t << 24) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+        for _ in range(8):
+            if crc & 0x80000000:
+                crc = (crc << 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+            else:
+                crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x04C11DB7) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+        tab[255 - t] = crc
+    data = (name + b"\0")[:33]
+    for b in data:
+        crc = tab[b ^ (crc >> 24)] ^ ((crc << 8) & 0xFFFFFF00)
+    return crc
+
+
+for a in sys.argv[1:]:
+    print("%-24s %08X" % (a or "(empty)", usba_crc32(bytes.fromhex(a))))
